open_points.subject: A20 JSON-depth measurement boundary
open_points.text: `json_depth_max` bounds every JSON value where it enters the kernel — a request, with every value, constant and schema it submits ...; a run input value nested exactly `json_depth_max` deep is accepted
open_points.question: Is depth measured on the complete request envelope, on each submitted logical value/schema/constant independently, or on both? A run input at depth 64 necessarily makes its enclosing request deeper than 64.
options: Measure each logical submitted value, constant and schema independently
Measure only the complete request message
Require both the complete request and each logical value to fit
open_points.default_guess: Measure each logical submitted value, constant and schema independently so the required exact-limit run-input case can pass.

open_points.subject: A20 request-check precedence
open_points.text: is checked there before any other walk of that value
open_points.question: For a request that is both over the depth limit and has an unknown token or another schema error, does the depth check precede token extraction and A16's fixed order, or does A16 remain size, token, schema with depth checked during schema validation?
options: Depth after size but before token handling
A16 remains authoritative: size, token, then depth/schema
Depth precedes even the request-size check
open_points.default_guess: Keep A16's order: size, token, then depth as the first schema-validation check.

open_points.subject: A20 object-depth definition
open_points.text: for an array or an object, one more than the deepest of its members
open_points.question: For an object, does “members” mean only member values, or do member names also participate in depth?
options: Only member values contribute
Both member names and values contribute
Each name/value pair is an extra container level
open_points.default_guess: Only member values contribute; object keys are not independently nested JSON values.

open_points.subject: A20 function-output depth
open_points.text: `json_depth_max` bounds every JSON value where it enters the kernel — ... a function's output — ... a function's output ... as its own decision says of an unrepresentable one
open_points.question: Is the limit applied to the returned output dictionary, to each value-port output independently, or both, especially when the dictionary also contains file-port `bytes`; and which A03 outcome records an over-depth value?
options: Check each value-port output independently and record `contract_violation`
Check the complete returned dictionary and record `contract_violation`
Check both the dictionary and each value-port output
Treat inability to measure/canonicalize as `crashed`
open_points.default_guess: Check each value-port output independently before schema validation and record `contract_violation`; do not treat file bytes as JSON.

open_points.subject: A20 service-answer depth
open_points.text: `json_depth_max` bounds every JSON value where it enters the kernel — ... a service's answer ... — and is checked there before any other walk of that value
open_points.question: For a JSON service response, is depth measured on the whole response object or on each bound output member, and does an over-depth response conclude `contract_violation` with an `applied` attempt for a non-read 2xx response?
options: Measure the whole parsed JSON body and classify it as `contract_violation`/`applied`
Measure each output member independently and classify it as `contract_violation`/`applied`
Measure both the body and members
Classify it as a malformed response, yielding `service_unreachable` or `outcome_unknown`
open_points.default_guess: Measure the whole parsed JSON body before member traversal and classify a 2xx violation as `contract_violation`, with a non-read attempt `applied`.

open_points.subject: A20 service bodies that A09 does not parse
open_points.text: `json_depth_max` bounds every JSON value where it enters the kernel — ... a service's answer ...; a binding without output ports ... does not parse or validate it; The body of an answer that is not used is not interpreted
open_points.question: Must the kernel parse JSON-looking bodies solely to enforce depth for bindings without outputs and for non-2xx answers, or does the depth rule apply only to response bodies A09 already parses as JSON outputs?
options: Apply depth only to bodies parsed as JSON outputs under A09
Parse every JSON-looking service body for depth even when A09 says not to interpret it
Treat every response body as JSON for the depth rule unless it is a declared file output
open_points.default_guess: Apply the depth limit only to bodies A09 parses as JSON outputs; leave unused and outputless bodies uninterpreted.

open_points.subject: A20 internally constructed JSON
open_points.text: `json_depth_max` bounds every JSON value where it enters the kernel ... A deeper value is a value JCS cannot represent ... `json_depth(value) <= json_depth_max`
open_points.question: Does the ceiling also govern JSON values constructed inside the kernel—mapped output arrays, HTTP JSON bodies, approval request descriptions, response envelopes, and the composite meaning facts canonicalized for identities—or only JSON crossing an ingress boundary?
options: Only ingress values are bounded; internal composites may be deeper
Every internal JSON composite is also bounded and may cause its enclosing operation to fail
Internal composites are bounded only when JCS hashing or storage is required
open_points.default_guess: Only ingress values are depth-checked; internal envelopes and composites may be deeper, otherwise accepted depth-64 inputs could not be wrapped, stored, hashed or returned consistently.

open_points.subject: A20 manifest and installation JSON
open_points.text: bounds every JSON value where it enters the kernel — a request, with every value, constant and schema it submits, a service's answer, a function's output
open_points.question: Does “every JSON value” include platform-manifest files and any JSON installation configuration, which also enter the kernel but are absent from the stated list; if so, which existing refusal or startup outcome represents an over-depth document?
options: Include manifest and configuration JSON, mapping depth excess to their existing parse/manifest failures
The list is exhaustive; manifest and configuration are not depth-bounded
Include manifest JSON but not installation configuration
open_points.default_guess: Include both and map depth excess to the same existing outcome as an unparseable configuration or manifest record.

open_points.subject: A20 earlier-release record exemption
open_points.text: every record stored under an earlier release — its values, constants and schemas — is read, executed with and returned as before
open_points.question: After `json_depth_max` is lowered, what happens when an exempt older deep value is passed through a function or service and re-enters as an otherwise equal output: is it still exempt because the run must execute and return it as before, or rejected because every function output and service answer is a new ingress?
options: The exemption follows the old stored value through execution and return when content is unchanged
Every function output or service answer is checked anew, even when it reproduces an old value
All outputs of runs using any earlier-release record use that record's former depth ceiling
open_points.default_guess: Exempt an unchanged value already stored under the earlier release, but depth-check genuinely new output values under the current release.
